evidence_excerpts: A review and meta-analysis commissioned by the U.S. Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality found that MBIs compared to active controls had a mixture of only moderate, low, or no efficacy depending on the disorder being treated.

The source reports moderate efficacy for reducing anxiety, depression, and pain symptoms; low efficacy for reducing stress and improving quality of life; and no effect or insufficient evidence for attention, positive mood, substance abuse, eating habits, sleep, and weight control.
text: Mindfulness-based interventions show mixed and condition-dependent clinical efficacy rather than uniformly strong therapeutic benefit.
